I now have a complete picture. Here are my findings.

## Summary

Note upfront: there is a clear mismatch between the acceptance-test spec ("identity-key-v2") and the current production implementation. The test expects `identityKey` to be a 64-char SHA-256 hex over `normalizedTelephone | lowerEmail | soundex(lastName)`, but the production `Owner.getIdentityKey()` returns a plain unhashed string with no soundex and no last name. There is no Soundex utility anywhere in the repo. Details below.

---

### 1. identityKey computation
File: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java` lines 132-139

```java
/** Derived duplicate-detection key: normalized telephone, email (or empty) and household id
 *  joined with '|'. ... */
@Transient
public String getIdentityKey() {
    return (this.telephone == null ? "" : this.telephone) + "|"
        + (this.email == null ? "" : this.email) + "|";
}
```

Reality vs. javadoc/spec: despite the comment mentioning "household id", the method concatenates only telephone and email (last `|` then empty). It does NOT hash (no SHA-256), does NOT include lastName, and does NOT include soundex. The SHA-256 hashing you expected lives instead in `CustomerCode`/`HouseholdId` (see below), not in the identity key.

### 2. Duplicate detection → HTTP 409 Conflict
File: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java` — method `addOwner`, lines 115-118

```java
if (owners.stream().anyMatch(existing -> existing.getIdentityKey().equals(owner.getIdentityKey()))
        || owners.stream().filter(existing -> existing.getCity().equalsIgnoreCase(owner.getCity())).count() >= 50) {
    return new ResponseEntity<>(HttpStatus.CONFLICT);
}
```

The candidate set is built at line 111 (`findAllOwners()` filtered to `!existing.isDeleted()`). A 409 is returned when an identity-key collision exists OR when the city already has ≥50 owners. There is a separate 429 quota check at lines 112-114.

Note: there is NO explicit "household-duplicate 409 block" — the household id is used only for counting members and membership capping (see item 4), not for a separate 409. The identity-key equality at line 115 is the only duplicate 409.

### 3. Soundex
No Soundex utility class or usage exists in production code. The only reference is in the test spec comment:
`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceTest.java` lines 9-11, which state the v2 identity key should incorporate `soundex(lastName)`. This is currently unimplemented — a soundex utility would need to be created.

### 4. householdId computation & household usage
Computation utility: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/HouseholdId.java` (full class), lines 37-53 — `of(lastName, postcode)` normalizes lastName (trim/collapse-space/lowercase, line 55-57), builds `normalize(lastName) + "|" + postcode`, SHA-256 hashes it, and returns the first 6 bytes as a 12-char uppercase hex string. Returns `null` if either input is null.

Accessor: `Owner.getHouseholdId()` at `Owner.java` lines 123-126 → `HouseholdId.of(getLastName(), this.postcode)`.

Usage in controller `OwnerRestControllerV1.java`:
- `sameHousehold(a, b)` helper, lines 143-147 (compares non-null equal household ids).
- Line 123: `owner.setHouseholdMemberCount(1 + count of existing owners in same household)`.
- Lines 129-135: household membership-level cap — computes max membership level among household members and caps the new owner's level to `householdMax + 1`.

There is no 409 tied to householdId (household is only counting/capping, not a hard-duplicate block).

### 5. Soft-match / possible-duplicate logic
File: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/PossibleDuplicate.java` (full class), lines 16-29. `of(owner, existing)` returns the id of the first existing owner matching: same postcode (case-insensitive) AND same lastName (case-insensitive) AND different telephone.

Important: this class is defined but NEVER called in production. `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner` hard-codes the opposite at lines 125-126:
```java
owner.setPossibleDuplicate(false);
owner.setPossibleDuplicateOf(null);
```
So soft-match is effectively dead code / unwired. The `Owner` fields/getters/setters are at `Owner.java` lines 82-86 and 171-188. Note the spec expected soundex(lastName)+postcode soft match, but `PossibleDuplicate.matches` uses exact case-insensitive lastName equality, not soundex.

### 6. Email-domain blocklist
Files:
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/validation/NonDisposableEmailValidator.java` (full class). Blocklist at lines 14-15: `Set.of("mailinator.com", "tempmail.com", "guerrillamail.com")`. Logic lines 18-27: null/blank or no `@` → valid; otherwise rejects if the lowercased domain (substring after last `@`) is in `BLOCKED`.
- Annotation: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/validation/NonDisposableEmail.java` (field-level constraint, `@Constraint(validatedBy = NonDisposableEmailValidator.class)`).

Email normalization also happens in `Owner.setEmail` (`Owner.java` lines 204-206) — lowercases the email.

### 7. Telephone normalization (normalizedTelephone)
Utility: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/PhoneNumbers.java` (full class).
- `toE164(raw)` lines 34-43: strips non-digits; if input had a `+`, returns `"+" + digits`; else assumes `+61`, dropping a single leading `0`.
- `toDisplay(e164)` lines 52-59: formats for humans grouped in threes.

Applied in `Owner.setTelephone` (`Owner.java` lines 264-266): `this.telephone = PhoneNumbers.toE164(telephone)`. The E.164 pattern constraint is on the field at `Owner.java` line 58 (`^\+[0-9]{8,15}$`). So the stored `telephone` is the "normalizedTelephone" fed into `getIdentityKey()` and `CustomerCode`.

Bonus — SHA-256 you were looking for: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/CustomerCode.java`, lines 38-42 and `hash8` lines 64-77 — builds `<REGION>-<HASH8>` where HASH8 = first 8 uppercase hex chars of `SHA-256(telephone + lastName)`. Invoked from `OwnerRestControllerV1.java` line 124.

### 8. Existing tests
File: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceTest.java` (full file, 29 lines):
- Class javadoc lines 9-11: documents the intended "identity-key-v2" spec (SHA-256 hex over normalizedTelephone | lowerEmail | soundex(lastName); duplicate → 409).
- `coreIdentityKeyIsSha256Hex()` lines 15-19: creates a `structuredOwner()`, fetches it, and asserts `identityKey` matches `[0-9a-f]{64}` (64 lowercase hex). This will FAIL against the current `Owner.getIdentityKey()` which returns a plain `tel|email|` string.
- `coreRejectsDuplicateIdentity()` lines 22-28: creates an owner, deep-copies it (identical telephone/email/lastName), and asserts the second create returns 409 Conflict.

Support file: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceBase.java` (322 lines). Relevant helpers:
- `structuredOwner()` lines 136-142 (uniqueLastName + addressLine1 + postcode "2000"), `ownerNode()` lines 117-125, `withPostcode()` 129-132.
- `createOwner()` lines 155-158, `createOwnerOk()` 160-162, `createOwnerWithKey()` (idempotency header) 165-168, `fillCity()` 173-179, `createMany()` 183+, `deleteOwner()` 195+.
- Unique generators lines 65-112 (`uniqueLastName`, `uniqueTelephone`, `uniqueEmail`, etc.).
- Crypto/oracle helpers: `sha256hex()` lines 282-294 (full lowercase hex — matches the shape the identityKey test expects), `shaHex(s,n)` lines 297-299 (first n uppercase hex — matches CustomerCode/HouseholdId shape), `luhn()` lines 302-321.

There are no dedicated unit tests for `HouseholdId`, `CustomerCode`, `PhoneNumbers`, `PossibleDuplicate`, or `NonDisposableEmailValidator` — only the two acceptance tests above exercise this area end-to-end.

---

### Key gaps if you intend to implement the v2 spec
- `Owner.getIdentityKey()` must be rewritten to SHA-256-hash `normalizedTelephone | lowerEmail | soundex(lastName)` and return 64-char lowercase hex.
- A Soundex utility class must be created (none exists).
- `PossibleDuplicate.of(...)` is implemented but unwired; the controller hard-codes `possibleDuplicate=false` at `OwnerRestControllerV1.java:125-126`. To enable soft-match, wire it in and switch its `matches()` from exact lastName equality to soundex+postcode.

The test expects `identityKey` to be a 64-char SHA-256 hex over `normalizedTelephone | lowerEmail | soundex(lastName)`, but the production `Owner.getIdentityKey()` returns a plain unhashed string with no soundex and no last name. File: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java` lines 132-139

```java

@Transient
public String getIdentityKey() {
    return (this.telephone == null ? "" : this.telephone) + "|"
        + (this.email == null ? "" : this.email) + "|";
}
```

Reality vs. javadoc/spec: despite the comment mentioning "household id", the method concatenates only telephone and email (last `|` then empty). It does NOT hash (no SHA-256), does NOT include lastName, and does NOT include soundex. ```

The candidate set is built at line 111 (`findAllOwners()` filtered to `!existing.isDeleted()`). A 409 is returned when an identity-key collision exists OR when the city already has ≥50 owners. There is a separate 429 quota check at lines 112-114.

Note: there is NO explicit "household-duplicate 409 block" — the household id is used only for counting members and membership capping (see item 4), not for a separate 409. The identity-key equality at line 115 is the only duplicate 409.
